newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian dies of rabies virus after bat scratch.
newsitem.headline: Australian dies of rabies virus after bat scratch.

text.p: An Australian woman who contracted a little-known strain of the rabies virus after being scratched by a fruit bat has died, health officials said on Saturday.
The 39-year-old, who contracted the virus two weeks ago after a scratch from a flying fox bat, died of encephalitis, or swelling of the brain, in a Brisbane hospital on Friday afternoon.
It was the first known case worldwide of a human being contracting the yet unnamed virus, which belongs to the Lyssavirus group that includes rabies.

The new virus was first identified earlier this year during a survey of native Australian fauna in a search for Equine morbillivirus, which killed a Queensland horse trainer and 14 horses in September 1994.
Queensland state Health Minister Mike Horan told reporters scientists were still in the dark about how the disease spread.
But he said people who handled the bats were being told to use protective clothing and those at risk were already receiving rabies vaccinations.

Last week, Australian Health Minister Michael Wooldridge said the Lyssavirus group representated a very low public risk in Australia, which is free of the more common form of rabies which causes muscular spasms, fever, uncontrollable excitement and extreme thirst.
"Although a new finding, it is likely this new virus strain has been present in Australian bat populations for thousands of years," Wooldridge said.
